transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-08 15:00 UTC — Duration: 48m
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Diego Ramos (Redwood), Maya Lin (ApexEdge), Rajiv Patel (ApexEdge), Hannah O'Neal (ApexEdge PM), Samir (ApexEdge Sec), Unidentified Speaker

[00:00] Alex Morgan: hey everyone thanks for joining, quick intro from our side — i'm alex, i'll run the account and priya here is our se who will lead the bench design. diego's on for any infra questions.
[00:14] Maya Lin: thanks alex, maya here. we're trying to validate a pilot to move our inference to the edge clusters, main goal is tight latency but also keep costs predictable.
[00:26] Priya Shah: great, that's helpful. one clarifying q up front — when you say edge are we talking small form-factor gpu nodes in regional colo or on-prem racks? that affects batching and cache strategy.
[00:38] Rajiv Patel: it's a mix — a few regional colo sites with 1-2 gpus per node, and a fallback central cluster. we expect traffic to be bursty during business hours; tails are long because of long conversational contexts.
[00:52] Alex Morgan: got it. high level agenda: define success criteria, pick SLOs (first token vs per-token), set p95/p99 targets, describe workload shape, and agree measurement plan.
[01:07] Hannah O'Neal: timeline question — we're aiming for a pilot to complete in four weeks; want go/no-go after bench runs and sample analysis.
[01:20] Diego Ramos: sounds doable but we should scope the measurement matrix carefully so we don't run ambiguous tests.
[01:30] Alex Morgan: ok let's talk SLO semantics — priya, can you give a quick on TTFT vs TPOT?
[01:36] Priya Shah: sure. TTFT (time-to-first-token) measures latency from request to first generated token — important for perceived latency in chat. TPOT (total-per-token) or per-token pacing measures steady-state throughput and cost per token; more sensitive to seq length and kv cache behavior. for edge use cases with short prompts TTFT often matters more, but if you have long contexts and streaming then TPOT is significant for cost and tail latencies.
[02:05] Rajiv Patel: we do have both — short user intents and also long context threads. i think we need both metrics. p95/p99 — what buckets do you recommend?
[02:15] Priya Shah: we typically propose: TTFT p95 <= 200ms, p99 <= 350ms for small models on dedicated GPUs; for larger models numbers shift up. TPOT often reported as p95/p99 per-token latency or tokens/sec under target load — for our pilots we run both single-request and burst concurrency sims.
[02:38] Maya Lin: 200ms p95 is quite aggressive for edge, is that realistic? some of our nodes are older.
[02:45] Diego Ramos: right, hardware variance matters — we can profile your fleet and categorize nodes. propose tiered SLOs: gold nodes p95 200ms, silver p95 350ms, fallback p95 500ms.
[02:58] Unidentified Speaker: (mumble) — the caches, do you mean KV cache?
[03:01] Priya Shah: yes KV cache — though the transcriber sometimes writes K-V as K V which gets confusing in docs. KV caching reduces token cost for repeated context but warms slowly on cold requests.
[03:16] Hannah O'Neal: for acceptance criteria we need concrete numbers we can sign off on. what does pass/fail look like?
[03:23] Alex Morgan: proposed acceptance matrix: 1) TTFT p95 within tiered targets for 95% of sampled traffic, 2) TPOT measured as median tokens/sec within 10% of expected and p99 less than threshold, 3) no more than 2% request error rate and graceful fallback to central cluster during overload.
[03:45] Rajiv Patel: how do you sample traffic? our production has spikes and long tails — we can't sample uniformly.
[03:52] Priya Shah: we ask for a 48h anonymized request dump including timestamps, payload size, seq lengths and user-agent if available. then we'll synthesize a traffic profile: baseline QPS, burst multipliers (x3, x5), and tail-length distribution.
[04:12] Maya Lin: we'll need an NDA for the export, security will scrub any pii.
[04:18] Samir Chaudhry: correct, we need to ensure data is anonymized and KMS keys are used if transfer is required. also SOC 2 docs — do you provide them?
[04:27] Alex Morgan: yes we have SOC2 and ISO attestation docs, we'll share our security pack. for private deployments we can integrate with customer KMS; diego can outline options.
[04:39] Diego Ramos: on private mode we support external KMS and HSM patterns; there are network egress constraints, need to know if you require air-gapped operation.
[04:50] Rajiv Patel: not air-gapped, but VPC peering only.
[04:53] Diego Ramos: noted.
[05:00] Priya Shah: back to measurement plan — we suggest a three-phase bench: 1) profiling (single-request cold/hot for sample nodes), 2) burst and steady-state runs (simulate baseline + bursts), 3) soak/test for error rates and fallback. each run should be repeated across node tiers.
[05:20] Hannah O'Neal: how long are each runs? we have limited credits for bench time.
[05:25] Priya Shah: profiling short — 10-15m per node. burst/steady-state 30-60m per config. soak could be 2-4 hours for reliability checks but we can compress to a 1h smoke for initial go/no-go.
[05:42] Maya Lin: I want to make sure we measure p95 and p99 correctly and not conflate network jitter.
[05:48] Alex Morgan: yes, measurement notes: collect server-side timestamps (ingress, start-gen, end-gen), client-side RTT, and compute SLOs using server-side timestamps, excluding known network jitter windows. we'll provide instrumentation hooks.
[06:06] Rajiv Patel: instrumenting the SDK is doable. what about multi-tenant variance? our nodes are shared with other teams.
[06:13] Diego Ramos: recommended to use isolated pilot nodes or reserved capacity; sharing leads to noisy neighbors — that should be a test dimension.
[06:22] Unidentified Speaker: do you support quantized kernels for older gpus?
[06:25] Priya Shah: yes we do int8/4 quant paths and specific kernel choices; the runtime will pick kernels based on seq length and model. we'll include quant profiles in the test matrix.
[06:37] Alex Morgan: let's put concrete SLO targets on the table for this pilot. given your hardware notes, propose tiered targets: Gold (newer colos): TTFT p95 250ms, p99 420ms; TPOT p95 per-token <= 8ms, p99 <= 15ms. Silver (older): TTFT p95 420ms, p99 700ms; TPOT p95 <= 14ms, p99 <= 30ms. Fallback central cluster: TTFT p95 <= 600ms.
[07:05] Maya Lin: can you justify those numbers — they sound optimistic for our oldest boxes.
[07:10] Priya Shah: numbers are based on similar pilots — we will run an initial profiling pass to calibrate and then adjust SLO buckets. the purpose is having measurable bands rather than a single one-size-fits-all.
[07:24] Rajiv Patel: sample rates — how do you compute p99 for TPOT when token counts vary per request?
[07:31] Priya Shah: two ways: normalized per-token latency (total gen time / tokens) for TPOT percentiles, and end-to-end per-request percentiles for TTFT. we'll include both in the matrix and present both medians and tail percentiles.
[07:46] Hannah O'Neal: what's the reporting cadence and dashboarding? we want per-route breakdowns.
[07:51] Alex Morgan: Redwood Console will produce per-route, per-model dashboards, token-level cost breakdown, and traces. we'll share a sample dashboard.
[07:59] Maya Lin: we also need to measure correctness/regression vs quality — you mentioned eval hooks?
[08:05] Priya Shah: yes run a quality sample: for a small set of prompts run golden outputs or scoring heuristics. quality regressions trigger alerts; we keep bench quality tied to prompt sets.
[08:16] Rajiv Patel: ok good. how do you handle fallback behavior in overload? do you degrade to smaller models or route to central?
[08:22] Alex Morgan: you can define routing policies — prefer smaller model, or fallback to central cluster, or queue with backpressure. part of the pilot is testing the chosen policy for user impact.
[08:35] Unidentified Speaker: side q — do you have docs comparing TTFT-first vs TPOT-first approaches?
[08:40] Priya Shah: yes we'll include an explainer doc; but in short TTFT-first is user-perceived latency centric, TPOT-first optimizes token cost and throughput. for chat, TTFT is often prioritized.
[08:54] Maya Lin: on instrumentation — you said server-side timing is important; we also need request IDs to correlate traces across our telemetry.
[08:59] Diego Ramos: yep include a request-id header in bench harness and logs; we'll map it to traces in console.
[09:07] Alex Morgan: timeline recap: prototype bench and profiling in week 1, run burst and soak in week 2, analyze and decision meeting in week 3, remediation and final report in week 4.
[09:19] Hannah O'Neal: would you be able to shorten to 3 weeks if we do an initial smoke and skip long soak?
[09:24] Priya Shah: yes we can do a 3-week fast-track with a 1h soak and a focus on the most common routes.
[09:30] Rajiv Patel: any estimated cost for bench runs? we need to budget.
[09:34] Alex Morgan: we'll send a bench cost estimate with the template; pilot credits can be discussed in commercial conversation.
[09:41] Maya Lin: security again — can the bench run without any egress? we need to keep logs inside VPC.
[09:47] Diego Ramos: bench controller can be deployed inside your VPC and results pushed to an s3-compatible bucket with KMS; we'll sign the access policy.
[09:59] Unidentified Speaker: (crosstalk) — what about measuring tail during bursts — we need to mimic real user think-time.
[10:04] Priya Shah: we'll use the traffic dump to synthesize think-time and inter-arrival distributions, incorporate burst windows and diurnal patterns.
[10:15] Alex Morgan: ok let's capture the acceptance criteria explicitly here:
[10:18] Priya Shah: Acceptance criteria (initial):
- TTFT p95 within selected tier band for 95% of sampled routes;
- TTFT p99 no more than 1.5x p95;
- TPOT median within 10% of expected baseline and TPOT p99 below tier threshold;
- Error rate < 2% sustained during baseline and < 5% during defined burst windows;
- Fallback behavior exercised with < 5% user-impactful errors.
[10:46] Maya Lin: can you put that in a table in the benchmark template?
[10:49] Alex Morgan: yes will include.
[10:51] Rajiv Patel: about long context — do we warm KV caches with a synthetic prefix?
[10:56] Priya Shah: yes tests include cold-start, warm with simulated user history, and prefix caching scenarios. warming strategy will be part of the harness.
[11:06] Hannah O'Neal: final question about metric windows — do you compute p99 on sliding windows or overall?
[11:11] Priya Shah: compute both: sliding (5m/1h) to detect transient regressions and global for the run. slide windows help identify burst-induced tail behavior.
[11:22] Samir Chaudhry: for compliance we need audit logs of bench runs and who accessed data.
[11:27] Diego Ramos: we'll provide audit trails and can seed logs into your SIEM.
[11:33] Alex Morgan: great. any other outstanding concerns?
[11:36] Maya Lin: timeline and security covered for now. we'll expect the NDA and bench template.
[11:41] Alex Morgan: recap of next steps: we'll share benchmark template/runbook and security pack by 3/11; maya exports traffic by 3/12; schedule orchestration kickoff week of 3/15. action items recorded in follow-up.
[11:56] Rajiv Patel: thanks everyone.
[12:00] Meeting ends.

Notes about transcript quality: automatic transcription has occasional mislabels and some technical terms mangled (e.g., KV cache shown as K V cache, TTFT occasionally transcribed as T T F T). The speaker labelled 'Unidentified Speaker' likely was a site ops engineer whose name didn't appear on calendar.

Bench plan (short):
- Inputs required: 48h anonymized request dump, model version, node specs, network latency matrix, KMS requirements.
- Profiling pass: cold/hot single request across node tiers, quantization profiles.
- Load pass: steady QPS at baseline, ramp to bursts (x3, x5), measure per-route TTFT/TPOT p95/p99 across windows.
- Soak pass: 1h smoke or 4h extended — measure error rates and fallback reliability.
- Reporting: dashboards for per-route p50 p95 p99, per-token cost breakdown, and a runbook with remediation actions.

References shared: "benchmark-template.xlsx" (will be attached), "security-pack-v2.pdf" link placeholder, sample dashboard screenshot sent in chat.

End of transcript.
